subtopic: Issuer Credit Risk and Limits of Principal Protection
source_evidence: Any promise to repay some or all of the money you invest will depend on the creditworthiness of the issuer of the note—meaning you could lose all of your money if the issuer of your note goes bankrupt.
answer: Principal protection on a structured note is not unconditional: repayment depends on the note issuer’s creditworthiness. If the issuer goes bankrupt, you could lose all of your investment, even when the product’s name suggests that principal is protected.
